correctionNotes: No published measurement exists (AutoEq, squig.link, Crinacle, 0db all checked on 2026-07-29). Every band here is a review-derived preference baseline, not a correction curve - keep moves modest and do not use narrow high-Q filters.
Open fit with no seal: sub-bass leaks out. Use a low shelf around 45-60 Hz to restore weight; do not chase sealed-IEM rumble.
Unlike the NH80, mid-bass is already slightly emphasized/bloomy, so pair the sub-bass shelf with a small 150-200 Hz trim instead of a mid-bass boost.
Lower mids are reported as slightly recessed/spread out; a gentle ~400 Hz lift restores body without adding mud.
Upper mids around 2-3 kHz are already forward (the 'V' of the V shape). Do not add Harman ear-gain here; a small trim is usually the better direction.
Treble varies a lot with foam/pad choice. Use a light 5.5-7 kHz cut for metallic glare and a gentle 10 kHz shelf for the air that Korean reviewers find lacking; re-evaluate whenever the foams change.
Sits below the NH60/NH80 in refinement, so avoid heavy corrective EQ that would expose its limits - prefer a tonal-balance pass.
signature: Affordable open flathead earbud with a mild V / upper-mid-forward voicing: punchy, slightly rich mid-bass that is unusually present for an earbud but still rolls off in the sub-bass because there is no seal; lower mids sit a little back; vocals (especially female) are clear and forward; treble is extended but described anywhere from politely restrained to mildly bright and metallic depending on foam/pad. 14.2 mm dynamic driver, 44 ohm, 115 dB.
